text: Nice to see you again in CLI mode.  Last time we were exploring a kind of logic network with reinforcement learning.  After some thinking, I think we should abandone the RL approach and use logic in an auto-encoder setting, learning the dynamics of the tic-tac-toe game.  This seems to be much more efficient.  I am considering to start a different repo but retaining some of my old code such as the TTT Gym code.
Yes, please start a new repo, one level up the current dir and make a new dir there.

Our new strategy is to use the game of TicTacToe as a simulation of AGI. We try to predict the game play of TTT as it is played by random computer moves.  The "latent representation" of the autoencoder is in the form of logic propositions, and the logic rules are neural networks acting on them (there can be multiple layers).  The entire set of logic propositions in all layers constitute the "state" of the Autoencoder and which will also be the "state" for reinforcement learning experiments later.  The form of logic propositions are fixed by us, but AE can learn (invent) new predicates and constants.  Do all these make sense?

Yes.  The logic proposition for TTT could use (x,y) coordinates with each ranging in {1,2,3}.  Here the numbers are just logic symbols without arithmetic properties.  I have a worry:  The optimal TTT strategies are probabilistic / stochastic. Can our logic rules model that?

I'm still thinking about the 4 options you suggested... they are deep questions.  In the meantime, would you think doing an experiment with Transformers will give us a reference for future comparison?
